tasks.title: Freeze API contracts and save invariants
tasks.goal: Specify implementation-ready request/response/error DTOs, entities, state revision/idempotency protocol, and offline settlement algorithm. Decide concrete local-session and rules-version handling without implementing game code.
acceptance: Each planned endpoint has method, payload, response, ownership checks and error cases; public versus account-private data is explicit.
Give worked 59/60/61-second, partitioned settlement, 8-hour cap, clock-rollback, retry and loadout-freeze examples with atomic transaction boundaries.
Define immutable arena snapshots, boss one-time claim, overflow conversion boundary, migration/reopen behavior and test clock/seed injection.
Record consistent package interfaces and no unresolved contract blocker for M1-02/M1-05/M1-07.

tasks.title: Specify combat, classes and bounded content
tasks.goal: Freeze exact combat formulas, action priorities, class/spec mechanics and stable content IDs. Use three classes, six specs, three normal enemies, one boss and at least nine base items/three affixes.
acceptance: Specify integer math, targeting/ties, speed order, cooldowns/status durations/stacking, healing, death, victory and timeout with worked examples.
Each specialization changes an observable outcome; define automatic ability behavior and unlock/switch rules.
Content tables include IDs, stats, slot restrictions, enemy compositions and boss behavior, with no runtime-ambiguous placeholders.
Align battle/reset/loadout rules with M1-01; leave reward values to the economy table rather than duplicating competing numbers.

tasks.title: Write original player-facing copy
tasks.goal: Deliver a compact keyed copy table for heroes/classes/specs/items/enemies/area/boss, onboarding and key result/error states. Keep names and flavor original.
acceptance: Every M1 content ID has a concise display name and useful description; no copied Idle Adventure text.
Include local-build explanation, first expedition guidance, offline cap, loadout lock, inventory overflow, boss reward and arena snapshot explanations.
Specify lengths suitable for narrow UI (short labels, short descriptions) and avoid lore that introduces extra mechanics.
Provide implementation-ready keys and no dangling content references.

tasks.title: Define progression and reward baseline
tasks.goal: Set exact levels 1-10 XP requirements, reward/drop/affix probabilities, boss first-clear reward, inventory overflow conversion and expected pacing. No shops or crafting.
acceptance: Tables/formulas have explicit units, probabilities summing correctly, rounding, caps and losses; XP per hero and level-up stat growth are unambiguous.
Show expected ordinary elapsed time to first gear, level 3 and boss readiness; label estimates pending simulation.
Specify the 100-unequipped-item limit and deterministic overflow behavior without deleting equipped gear.
Specify non-exploitable one-time boss reward and zero arena rewards; match offline cycle/cap semantics.

tasks.title: Scaffold local workspace and verification commands
tasks.goal: Create the npm TypeScript workspace, tested runtime/dependency versions, minimal React shell/Fastify health route, lint-free typecheck/test/build setup and a reliable Windows local launcher. Preserve existing planning scripts/documents.
acceptance: Document tested Node/npm versions and compatible dependencies; npm ci, typecheck, minimal tests and build pass.
npm run dev starts UI/API on 5174/3100 with configurable ports; health and browser shell work without cloud services.
Port conflict and shutdown behavior are exercised; no hidden external service or global package-manager requirement.
README accurately distinguishes working commands from later ones; game state remains server-owned in the skeleton.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic combat and content validation
tasks.goal: Encode validated content and implement pure seeded combat, effective stats, XP/level helpers and reward generation using the frozen rules. Keep clock/storage/UI out of the engine.
acceptance: Same inputs/seed/version yield identical outputs; tests cover targeting ties, dead actors, healing/status behavior and 100-round timeout.
Three classes and six specs are encoded and each spec has a behavior test; invalid content and references fail clearly.
Item instance/affix generation and XP helpers match economy tables with deterministic rounding and bounded results.
Logs have structured events and bounded retention; no Date.now, database/browser imports or unseeded randomness inside rules.

tasks.title: Implement SQLite saves and isolated local sessions
tasks.goal: Implement migrations/repositories, seed two local accounts, opaque cookie sessions, ownership enforcement, state revisions and transactional idempotency infrastructure.
acceptance: Fresh database and save reopen/migration pass using isolated fixtures; test data never replaces real saves.
Local account selection/current session/logout work in two independent sessions; private cross-account access/mutation is rejected.
Same-request retries return stored results, changed-payload reuse and stale revisions fail, concurrent mutations remain atomic.
Loopback default, validated payload limits, session cookie handling and consistent API error contract are verified.

tasks.title: Implement expedition, gear and offline progression
tasks.goal: Wire party/equipment/spec actions, expedition start/settle/stop, capped offline rewards, XP/loot/overflow and boss first-clear reward through authoritative atomic services.
acceptance: 59/60/61-second, partitioned, negative elapsed, 8-hour cap and repeated-cap fixtures match the contract; downtime/reopen preserves state/seed/remainder.
Repeated and concurrent settlement cannot duplicate rewards; inventory and checkpoint commit together.
Party ownership/distinctness, wrong-slot/double equip and active-expedition loadout/spec lock are enforced server-side.
Boss first-win reward is atomic and cannot be farmed; overflow conversion is correct; bounded catch-up and logs are implemented.

tasks.title: Specify interface flows and accessible states
tasks.goal: Produce an implementation-ready compact screen/state map and component inventory for the first-playable loop. Use text/CSS fallbacks; no separate asset generation.
acceptance: Every screen/action maps to real contract endpoints and copy keys, including result/retry/conflict states.
Keyboard/focus behavior, desktop/narrow layout and disabled-action explanations are specified.
Gear comparison, specialization choice, credited/discarded offline time and snapshot version are understandable without developer jargon.
No new game system or mandatory art dependency is introduced.

tasks.title: Build the playable browser interface
tasks.goal: Implement all M1 screens against real endpoints: local session, party/spec/gear, expedition/log/rewards, boss and asynchronous arena. Make the complete loop usable with text and CSS.
acceptance: A browser can complete the main loop with real persisted server state; no hard-coded success, fake reward or disconnected placeholder buttons.
Required loading/empty/error/reconnect/conflict states work; repeated submission is handled without losing context.
Keyboard actions/focus and 1280x720/390px layouts are inspected; contrast and accessible labels are checked.
Optional portraits/icons have usable fallbacks; combat presentation never controls authoritative outcomes.

tasks.title: Implement immutable asynchronous arena battles
tasks.goal: Add publish/list snapshot, challenge and private battle-report endpoints. Simulate with production combat against an immutable opponent team and persist reproducible reports.
acceptance: Two local accounts publish and challenge without the defender being online; only intended public snapshot fields are exposed.
Changing defender gear/spec later cannot alter a stored snapshot or report; save/restart preserves reports.
Request retries are idempotent and foreign private report retrieval is rejected; opponent live state is never modified.
Reports include seed/rules/snapshot versions and outcome; timeout is draw and no arena rewards/ranking are introduced.

tasks.title: Add seeded pacing and catch-up benchmarks
tasks.goal: Provide npm run simulate with explicit seeds/runs using the production engine, and a repeatable eight-hour settlement benchmark. Avoid duplicating combat/progression formulas.
acceptance: Fixed seed reproduces results; multiple seeds and specialization choices report distributions for gear, level 3 and boss readiness.
Results include assumptions, simulated elapsed time, win/loss counts and version/seed identifiers.
Eight-hour catch-up measures time/memory/log bound and responsiveness on recorded hardware/runtime; target from QA plan is assessed honestly.
Command has bounded output, supports saving machine-readable results, and never mutates a real player database.

tasks.title: Tune first-session pacing from simulation evidence
tasks.goal: Inspect measured baseline and prescribe minimal numeric changes with expected effects. Keep changes inside the same content budget and send exact table deltas to M1-14.
acceptance: Evidence covers multiple fixed seeds and builds; pacing targets versus observed distribution are explicit.
Recommend exact before/after values or justify no change; avoid speculative new systems to fix tuning.
Explain effects on offline rewards, loss streaks, boss readiness and viable specializations.
Define a focused rerun for M1-14 to verify the applied changes without repeating unrelated checks.

tasks.title: Integrate, harden and prepare the local release candidate
tasks.goal: Apply reviewed tuning, resolve integration defects, serve the built client locally and document the complete launch/save/test workflow. Produce a release candidate for independent QA.
acceptance: Applied tuning matches design and focused simulation rerun measures the intended effect; no hidden mechanical changes.
Fresh npm ci, validate and full browser walkthrough pass or failures are fixed; built client is served locally by the API.
README covers prerequisites, commands, ports, data location, backup/reset safeguards, two-account testing and local-only auth limitations.
Record reproducible build/test evidence and remaining defects; no P0/P1 issue is knowingly passed to release as acceptable.

tasks.title: Independently verify first-playable acceptance
tasks.goal: Exercise A01-A13 independently against the integrated game, add focused end-to-end regression coverage and provide release evidence. File concrete defects to existing task owners; do not silently fix gameplay code.
acceptance: Each A01-A13 has pass/fail/blocked and concrete evidence; no invented or unrun test is marked pass.
Two browser contexts, retry/concurrency/ownership attacks, restart/cap behavior and one-time boss rewards are verified.
Keyboard and both viewport sizes are inspected with screenshots or explicit observations; empty/error/reconnect flows are included.
Report contains reproducible defects/severity and a clear release recommendation; P0/P1 defects keep this task incomplete.

tasks.title: Review playability and accept the first milestone
tasks.goal: Review QA, pacing and the actual local game against the owner promise. Write the concise milestone verdict and owner playtest instructions; distinguish working functionality from subjective enjoyment.
acceptance: Verdict references A01-A13 and actual QA/pacing evidence, with no unresolved P0/P1 issue treated as accepted.
Owner can launch and follow a short playtest without reading technical documents.
State what is implemented, known limitations and any focused P2 follow-up; do not fabricate player feedback or claim commercial readiness.
If rejected, identify the existing task(s) to reopen and the precise failed gate; if accepted, mark the milestone verdict complete.
